details:
We need to do something about mods. I overheard some hackers talk about how they continued to crash game lobbies and by pass perma-bans. I have screenshot of these people, I won't reveal their identifications unless absolutely necessary. Mods continue to ruining the experience for many. They are using outdated versions of VRChat that can still support running the game online. They are also using pirated versions of the game to apparently use it's API, client, or APK data. There are apparently multiple mods out there. They listed six, I can't remember their names. According to what I overheard, these hackers brag about crashing lobbies, crashing people, and take joy in crashing multiple lobbies a day, getting banned and returning a couple of hours later or the next day to do it all over again. It's ridiculous and these mods need to stop. My solution would be to investigate the source of what mods they are using, how to find and detect them, what out dated versions of VRChat they are using, how are they using them, and identifying what pirated versions of VRChat they can use for the API (or APK). Overall, it would make VRChat more enjoyable if malicious mods didn't exist. 

To add to that, it would also be handy to find somehow ways to detect mod users. Perhaps show what version of VRChat they are using internally or server side. I like the idea of having access to logs on what is happening in the world (when the players enable it in a menu) they can see what players are doing. If a person does get crashed by someone, they can have a list of names and activities to see who did it, how it happened, and what happened and keep log-evidence for a report. Players need individual tools they can use to submit with evidence for a report of players using malicious mods.
title: Mod Methods, Detection, and Malicious Activity Logs for Evidence in Mod Reports
